The '''Electronic Literature Lab''', housed in [[Washington State University Vancouver|Washington State University, Vancouver]], maintains obsolete computers and hardware to preserve and present early [[electronic literature]], [[Video game|video games]], and internet works such as Instagram zines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Germain |first=Thomas |date=2025-05-18 |title=Still booting after all these years: The people stuck using ancient Windows computers |url=https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20250516-the-people-stuck-using-ancient-windows-computers |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref> It was founded in 2011 by [[Dene Grigar]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/electronic-literature-lab/history.html |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=dtc-wsuv.org}}</ref>
[[File:Electronic literature lab space.jpg|thumb|Part of the Electronic Literature Lab housed in the Washington State University at Vancouver]]

== Laboratory description ==
The Electronic Literature Lab holds the hardware and software that the [[The NEXT Museum|NEXT Museum, Library, and Preservation Space]] depends on to show electronic literature works in their original environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Electronic Literature Lab (ELL) {{!}} ELMCIP |url=https://elmcip.net/organizations/electronic-literature-lab-ell |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=elmcip.net}}</ref>  The lab forms the center of archiving electronic literature for the [[Electronic Literature Organization]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grigar |first=Dene |date=May 2019 |title=Archiving Electronic Literature: Selection Criteria, Methodology, and Challenges |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333126605 |journal=Journal of Archival Organization |volume=15 |issue=1–2 |pages=20–33 |doi=10.1080/15332748.2019.1609310}}</ref> Because electronic literature works were built on specific hardware, software, and platforms, these works are now largely inaccessible as hardware and software becomes obsolete.<ref>{{Cite web |last=culturalstudiesleuven |date=2018-07-02 |title=Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing |url=https://culturalstudiesleuven.net/2018/07/02/traversals-the-use-of-preservation-for-early-electronic-writing/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Cultural Studies Leuven |language=en}}</ref> Thus the lab maintains over 80 [[Vintage computer|vintage computers]] from 1977 onwards<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/electronic-literature-lab/index.html |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=dtc-wsuv.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=webmaster |date=2025-05-19 |title=La tecnología que se negó a morir: cómo Windows XP, DOS y otros fantasmas digitales aún gobiernan el mundo |url=https://mimanizalesdelalma.com/internacional/la-tecnologia-que-se-nego-a-morir-como-windows-xp-dos-y-otros-fantasmas-digitales-aun-gobiernan-el-mundo/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=mi Manizales del alma! |language=es}}</ref> to serve over 3,000<ref>{{Cite web |last=EBonline |title=Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://earlybirds.io/listings/2183121-Electronic%20Literature%20Lab |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=EarlyBirds Open Innovation Ecosystem |language=en}}</ref> works of electronic literature<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pathfinders: Collection of Early Digital Literature in the Electronic Literature Lab (ELL) |url=https://scalar.usc.edu/works/pathfinders/the-electronic-literature-collection |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Pathfinders |language=en}}</ref> for researchers to analyze, such as the over 60 works from [[Marjorie Luesebrink|M.D. Coverley.]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lillvis |first1=Kristen |last2=White |first2=Melinda |date=2023-08-28 |title=Review: Marjorie C. Luesebrink Collection at ELO's The NEXT |url=https://reviewsindh.pubpub.org/pub/marjorie-c-luesebrink-collection/release/1 |journal=Reviews in Digital Humanities |language=en |volume=IV |issue=8 |doi=10.21428/3e88f64f.fb0bd342 |issn=2766-9297}}</ref> The lab also hosts video games, such as ''[[Amnesia (1986 video game)|Amnesia]]'' (1986).<ref>{{Cite web |title=fireworks24 added AMNESIA: Restored to Computer |url=https://itch.io/e/30084438/fireworks24-added-to-computer |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=itch.io |language=en}}</ref>

This lab has been called unique as it is "a  reading room preserves literature, art and games created on computers that cannot be printed."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-01 |title=WSUV's Electronic Literature Lab 'the only place in the world that does born-digital conservation' |url=https://www.columbian.com/news/2025/jul/28/wsuvs-electronic-literature-lab-the-only-place-in-the-world-that-does-born-digital-conservation/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=The Columbian |language=en-US}}</ref> James O'Sullivan called it "what is possibly the greatest collection of first-generation e-lit in the Western world."<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=O'Sullivan|first1=James|author-link1=James O'Sullivan (academic)|date=2017-11-07|location=[[Los Angeles]]|title=Electronic Literature's Contemporary Moment: Breeze and Campbell's "All the Delicate Duplicates"|url=https://lareviewofbooks.org/article/electronic-literature-turns-a-new-page-breeze-and-campbells-all-the-delicate-duplicates|magazine=[[Los Angeles Review of Books]]|language=en-us|oclc=904358349|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250816152955/https://lareviewofbooks.org/article/electronic-literature-turns-a-new-page-breeze-and-campbells-all-the-delicate-duplicates|archive-date=2025-08-16|access-date=2025-09-10}}</ref> As Kristin Lillvis and Melinda White note, "the Electronic Literature Lab has preserved many of these works in the collection through restoration processes involving migration and emulation to make them once-again accessible."<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lillvis |first1=Kristen |last2=White |first2=Melinda |date=2023-08-28 |title=Review: Marjorie C. Luesebrink Collection at ELO's The NEXT |url=https://reviewsindh.pubpub.org/pub/marjorie-c-luesebrink-collection/release/1 |journal=Reviews in Digital Humanities |language=en |volume=IV |issue=8 |doi=10.21428/3e88f64f.fb0bd342 |issn=2766-9297}}</ref> The lab documents these archival processes in scholarly publications such as ''The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction'' (2023)<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grigar |first1=Dene |last2=Pisarski |first2=Mariusz |date=February 2024 |title=The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction: Editions, Translations, and Emulations |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/elements/abs/challenges-of-borndigital-fiction/D7C93C1C77F8ED920D86234E00AF1448 |journal=Elements in Digital Literary Studies |language=en |doi=10.1017/9781009181488|isbn=978-1-009-18148-8 }}</ref> and ''Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing'' (2018).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stuart |first1=Moulthrop|last2=Dene |first2=Grigar|last3=Joseph |first3=Tabbi|date=2017-04-07 |title=Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing |url=https://academic.oup.com/mit-press-scholarship-online/book/30669 |journal=OUP Academic |language=en |doi=10.7551/mitpre|doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 }}</ref> 

[[Dene Grigar]] founded and directs this lab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Electronic Literature Lab {{!}} Washington State University |url=https://vancouver.labs.wsu.edu/grigar-ell/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=vancouver.labs.wsu.edu}}</ref> She describes her theory of preservation for electronic items in her 2025 [[Ted Talk]] ''Making the Virtual Real and the Real Virtual.''<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QG_v7hiLwAk |title=Making the Virtual Real and the Real Virtual {{!}} Dene Grigar {{!}} TEDxMarshallU |date=2025-04-09 |last=TEDx Talks |access-date=2025-05-26 |via=YouTube}}</ref> As [[Jan Baetens|Jan Beatens]] explained, [[Stuart Moulthrop]] and [[Dene Grigar]] explicate the challenges in this pioneering field of preserving electronic literature in the Electronic Literature Lab.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-01 |title=Review of Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing |url=https://leonardo.info/review/2018/07/review-of-traversals-the-use-of-preservation-for-early-electronic-writing |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Leonardo/ISASTwith Arizona State University |language=en}}</ref> Part of this work is interviews with pioneers in the electronic literature field such as  Bob Stein, founder of [[Voyageur Press|Voyager Press]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A7c_cFQ3A6g |title=Electronic Literature Lab: Interview with Bob Stein of Voyager |date=2019-10-31 |last=Electronic Literature Lab (ELL) |access-date=2025-08-23 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

This is a working research lab as "Kristin Lillvis and Melinda White note: "even more significantly, the Electronic Literature Lab has preserved many of these works in the collection through restoration processes involving migration and emulation to make them once-again accessible."<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lillvis |first1=Kristen |last2=White |first2=Melinda |date=2023-08-28 |title=Review: Marjorie C. Luesebrink Collection at ELO's The NEXT |url=https://reviewsindh.pubpub.org/pub/marjorie-c-luesebrink-collection/release/1 |journal=Reviews in Digital Humanities |language=en |volume=IV |issue=8 |doi=10.21428/3e88f64f.fb0bd342 |issn=2766-9297}}</ref> ELL hosts online events such as the ''List of 280 Women E-Lit Pioneers & Visionaries (1985-2020).''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nuestras voces en la historia de la literatura electrónica |url=https://centroculturadigital.mx/revista/nuestras-voces-en-la-historia-de-la-literatura-electronica |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=centroculturadigital.mx}}</ref> The lab has hosted post-graduate students and research studies into born digital works.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Rebooting Electronic Literature: About the Electronic Literature Lab and Its Library of Electronic Media |url=https://scalar.usc.edu/works/rebooting-electronic-literature/about-the-electronic-literature-lab-and-its-library-of-electronic-media |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Rebooting Electronic Literature: Documenting Pre-Web Born Digital Media |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pawlicka-Deger |first=Urszula |title=research {{!}} Urszula Pawlicka-Deger |url=https://www.pawlickadeger.com/_pages/research/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=www.pawlickadeger.com |language=en}}</ref> Electronic literature  critics, such as [[Astrid Ensslin]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Digital Histories: A review of Astrid Ensslin's Pre-web Digital Publishing and the Lore of Electronic Literature {{!}} ebr |url=https://electronicbookreview.com/publications/digital-histories-a-review-of-astrid-ensslins-pre-web-digital-publishing-and-the-lore-of-electronic-literature/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=electronicbookreview.com |language=en}}</ref> and [[Mariusz Pisarski]], have collaborated with WSUV students and professors to analyze and archive electronic literature works.<ref>{{Cite web |title=International scholars join Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://cas.wsu.edu/2020/09/09/international-scholars-join-electronic-literature-lab/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=College of Arts and Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref> The works from the lab were exhibited at the Library of Congress in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ashenfelder |first=Mike |date=2013-11-13 |title=Preserving Vintage Electronic Literature {{!}} The Signal |url=https://blogs.loc.gov/thesignal/2013/11/preserving-vintage-electronic-literature |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=The Library of Congress}}</ref>  

== Awards and grants ==
The lab received an Open Scholarship Award from the Canadian Social Knowledge Institute in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Open Scholarship Awards {{!}} Electronic Textual Cultures Lab |url=https://etcl.uvic.ca/2022/01/25/2022-open-scholarship-awards/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=etcl.uvic.ca}}</ref>

Other grant and award-winning studies at the lab included  ''Chronicles: Documenting the Articulation of Culture in Video Games (2016)'', by Madeleine Brookman which garnered WSUV's 2016 Emeritus Society Undergraduate Research Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Undergraduate Research Award Winners {{!}} Emerita/Emeritus Society {{!}} Washington State University |url=https://emeritussociety.wsu.edu/2016-undergraduate-research-award-winners/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=emeritussociety.wsu.edu}}</ref> the 2015 CAS Summer Mini-Grant, and the 2014-5 Auvril Fellowship.<ref name=":0" />
